commit_subject: (screen-flagged) b1.6 (PR #1300): removes hard-coded exemplar entry_is_line_a..e derived rules (proof atoms citing other chapters' HTS lines) from every generated chapter and makes them caller inputs; summary claims runtime semantics unchanged — unsure, part of the same decoupling repair.
description: The identifiers entry_is_line_a, entry_is_line_b, entry_is_line_c, entry_is_line_d, and entry_is_line_e are caller inputs supplied by entry preparation from incidence classification.

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: Chapter 91's composition gated its §301/§201/§232-aluminum/§338 components on equality against five HTS lines from other chapters, so the gates were constant false for any 91xx entry and the components were dead, with proof atoms citing provisions outside this chapter.
triage.triage_notes: Same pattern as index 84; odd-chapter placement variant (45 redundant parenthesis pairs, `from:` temporal spelling). Same caveats as index 84.
triage.verifier_justification: The ch86 diff deletes five derived rules whose formulas were equality against single out-of-chapter statistical reporting numbers (7202.11.10.00, 7601.10.30.00, 9506.62.40.40, 2203.00.00.30, 8541.42.00.10), each with proof atoms citing those other chapters' provisions, and makes the identifiers caller inputs — so this is a change to the module's computed values and input surface, not proof/metadata bookkeeping. Because an hts_number classified in chapter 86 can never equal any of those five lines, every gate was constant false pre-fix, which forced china_section_301_component_rate (`if entry_is_line_a and origin_is_china: list_1_... + ... + if entry_is_line_e ...`), section_201_component_rate, the §232 aluminum/beer chain and the §338 gate to zero for all chapter-86 entries. I checked the pinned corpus release (us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap) and HTS chapter 99 U.S. note 20(b) and 20(d) — the enumerations for headings 9903.88.01/9903.88.02 — do list chapter-86 subheadings (8601.10.00, 8601.20.00, 8602.10.00, 8603.x, 8604.00.00, 8605.00.00, 8606.x, 8607.x), so the identically-zero §301 output contradicted the source rather than harmlessly matching it. The branch condition had no basis in the provisions this module encodes and the fix removes it, which is untraceable_branch (a formula grounded on the wrong provision); alternatives fail — nothing is inverted (polarity_or_logic), no clause is added (unrepresented_clause), and no amount or window moved.
triage.verifier_notes: inferred from verified sibling module index 84 (same kind and rule path in this chunk). Refutation attempts and what survived: (1) "mechanical" fails — five rules with formulas, dtypes, effective windows and proof atoms are deleted and the identifiers become caller inputs; the post summary itself says they "are caller inputs supplied by entry preparation from incidence classification." (2) "not_a_defect / new coverage never claimed" fails — the module is the chapter-86 statutory stack (it imports ch86's own rate table and does `ch86_general_rate[hts_line]`), so it claims to serve chapter-86 entries, and its §301/§201/§232/§338 components were live outputs that could only ever fire on other chapters' lines. (3) The generator boilerplate "Values, dates, dtypes, proof atoms, and runtime semantics are unchanged" is stale text describing the sibling-distinctness serialization (redundant parens, chapter-prefixed scalars) relative to the witness, not this change; the screener was right to be unsure of it. Caveats for the reviewer: this identical repair lands in ~100 generated chapter modules in one commit (tools/generate_schedule_compositions.py is the real edit), so the corpus will hold ~100 near-duplicate instances of this one defect — dedupe to one representative. The repair is also partial at this commit: post-fix, china_section_301_component_rate still carries proof atoms citing 7202.11.10.00 / 9506.62.40 / 7601.10.30.00 / 2203.00.00 / 8541.42.00, section_122 still reads `if entry_is_line_a or entry_is_line_b: 0`, and module source_verification still lists the five out-of-chapter citation paths; the §122 decoupling and the steel component described in the PR body are in other commits of PR #1300. PR body language supporting fidelity (not this file's diff): "the witness's exemplar coupling, which round-2 evaluation showed unlawfully suppressed the surcharge on §301-member lines for all origins".
